newsitem.title: USA: Walbro sees Q4 earnings below estimates.
newsitem.headline: Walbro sees Q4 earnings below estimates.

text.p: Walbro Corp said Monday its earnings for the 1996 fourth quarter and full year are likely to be below analysts' estimates.

"Weak passenger car sales in Europe, the strong dollar and continued insourcing of products by a major domestic customer affected profits from automotive operations in the fourth quarter," L.E. Althaver, chairman, said in a statement.
Althaver said several factors that affected third quarter earnings continued into the fourth quarter.

"As previously noted, production at Walbro Automotive's new plastic fuel tank facility in Brazil did not begin in the third quarter as planned," he said. "While production did begin in the fourth quarter, the customer-scheduled ramp-up was below expected levels and affected margins."
Walbro did not give specific earnings estimates. Asked about estimates, Chief Financial Officer Michael Shope referred to First Call, which shows a consensus fourth quarter estimate of $0.32 a share.
The fourth quarter estimate range is $0.25 to $0.45 a share, compared with year-ago earnings of $0.30.
For all of 1996, the mean earnings estimate is $1.66 a share, based on a range of $1.60 to $1.80, according to First Call. In 1995 Walbro earned $1.61 a share.

"Production at Walbro Engine Management's new carburetor plant in China is increasing more slowly than planned, with shipments remaining below scheduled levels in the fourth quarter," Althaver said. "In addition, worldwide orders for lawn-and-garden products did not rebound as expected in the fourth quarter due to carry-over of customer inventory."
Althaver said the outlook for 1997 remains positive, based in part on new plastic fuel tank programs that will start in the second half of the year.
Walbro makes precision fuel systems and products for the autmotive and small engine markets.
